title: LIPITOR (atorvastatin calcium) tablets, for oral use: full prescribing information
authors: US Food and Drug Administration (labelling submitted by Viatris Specialty LLC)
journal: US Food and Drug Administration approved prescribing information, via DailyMed; version 8, effective 15 April 2024
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement
result: Mechanism of action: atorvastatin is a selective, competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme that converts HMG-CoA to mevalonate, a precursor of sterols including cholesterol; in animal models it lowers plasma cholesterol by inhibiting hepatic HMG-CoA reductase and cholesterol synthesis and by increasing hepatic cell-surface LDL receptors. Absorption: absolute bioavailability of the parent drug about 14% and systemic availability of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitory activity about 30%, the low systemic availability being attributed to presystemic clearance in gastrointestinal mucosa and/or hepatic first-pass metabolism. Atorvastatin is extensively metabolised to ortho- and parahydroxylated derivatives that inhibit HMG-CoA reductase equivalently, and about 70% of circulating inhibitory activity is attributed to active metabolites; in vitro studies suggest the importance of metabolism by CYP3A4. Elimination is primarily biliary; plasma half-life about 14 hours, half-life of inhibitory activity 20 to 30 hours; less than 2% of a dose appears in urine. Atorvastatin is a substrate of the hepatic transporters OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 and of the efflux transporter BCRP. Ciclosporin raised atorvastatin AUC 8.69-fold and Cmax 10.66-fold.
